reason: Slack's free plan already handles our chat, and half of what we coordinate happens in voice notes, which this doesn't even mention. Flat $20 for two is fairer than per-seat pricing, but I'd be paying to move tools we already have for free, and I doubt my partner would open it every day.
objection: We'd both have to switch everything over and use it daily. If one of us drifts back to Slack and voice notes, I'm paying $240 a year for a fancy task list.
would_change_my_mind: If it handled voice notes well, letting us record, transcribe and turn them into tasks right next to the work, and it clearly replaced a paid tool we cancel, I'd try the free trial with my partner.
